what does detections do and what do you mean by replans?

content.text:
**Detections** are rules you set up once in neatlogs that automatically check every trace and flag the ones that match. Without them you have to open traces one by one to spot a problem; with them, the trace list marks the bad runs for you in its Detections column.

The four I suggested each watch for a different thing:

| Detection | What it flags |
|---|---|
| Regex `closed right now` | Any run where the verifier refused a venue for being closed |
| Regex `scout used the default query` | Any run where the model call failed and the scout fell back to a canned search |
| Condition: more than 2 LLM calls, or latency above 4 s | Runs that are slow or wasteful, which is the bug we fixed |
| PII on prompts | Personal data being sent to the model |

They matter for the hackathon because using Detections is part of the neatlogs tool-use score: it shows you monitor the agent, not just look at it once.

**Replans** are OOO's second and third attempts within one run. The flow is:

1. The scout finds places.
2. The verifier checks each one (real, open now, where the reel says).
3. If none pass, the run goes back to the scout to look again. That trip back is a replan.
4. After two replans with nothing passing, the run ends and sends no nudge.

The bug in your before trace was that the replans weren't really looking again: each one repeated the same 15 km search and got the same refused places. After the fix, each replan widens the search (15 km, then 37.5 km, then 60 km) without calling the model.

On your screenshot: yes, it works as the before picture. It shows the 38 steps, the 5.4 s, and the first model call asking for a sunset spot within 15 km. I was about to copy it into `evidence/` and add it to the README when you stopped the command, so it isn't added yet. Say the word and I'll do that.

PII stands for **personally identifiable information**: anything that can identify a specific person, such as a name, phone number, email address, home address, ID number or exact location.

A PII detection scans what gets sent to the model and flags any run where that kind of data appears.

It matters for OOO because the bot handles exactly this sort of data. A traveller chats with it on Telegram and shares their live location, and their messages may mention a phone number or where they're staying. The detection tells you when that ends up in a prompt to the model, so you know what personal data is leaving your system.

For the hackathon it's also one of the detection types the build plan lists, and it shows the judges you thought about privacy, not only about speed and cost.

On 2026-10-12 the user asked me to remember every neatlogs error and piece of feedback from the build, because they will send it to the neatlogs team as feedback. Add to this list whenever a new one comes up.

1. LangGraph auto-instrumentation split one run into 22 separate traces; model, tool and guardrail spans inside a graph node lost their parent. Worked around by turning it off and tracing graph steps with our own spans (commit `1c3242f`).
2. Model `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` via OpenRouter is `pricing_status: unpriced` / `unknown_model` in trace exports, so no per-run cost. The app UI later showed about $0.0001 per call on the same trace.
3. No public or shareable link for a single trace; docs describe only team visibility. Judges needing a login was a worry until the mentor said links plus screenshots are accepted.
4. New detection, Configure step: "Preview failed" for a valid regex (`closed right now`, span-level, scope verifier). The detection worked after saving; backfill flagged 88 spans.
5. Editing a detection returned `"error": "AI service error"`.
6. Editing a detection (changing only the name) fails on "Update detection" with "Request failed with status code 422"; no field is marked invalid. Creating works.
7. The neatlogs CLI trace reader needs a separate service-account token, so a trace could not be read from the terminal with the project API key.
8. A run that ends with no nudge shows status "success"; nothing marks a silent run without a custom detection.
9. Investigate ("Ask neat AI") assumed two unchecked venues were valid when the fixture data showed they were not.

**Why:** feedback to neatlogs is part of the hackathon relationship; the user wants it collected in one place.

On 2026-10-12 the user asked me to remember every neatlogs error and piece of feedback from the build, because they will send it to the neatlogs team as feedback. Add to this list whenever a new one comes up.

1. LangGraph auto-instrumentation split one run into 22 separate traces; model, tool and guardrail spans inside a graph node lost their parent. Worked around by turning it off and tracing graph steps with our own spans (commit `1c3242f`).
2. Model `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` via OpenRouter is `pricing_status: unpriced` / `unknown_model` in trace exports, so no per-run cost. The app UI later showed about $0.0001 per call on the same trace.
3. No public or shareable link for a single trace; docs describe only team visibility. Judges needing a login was a worry until the mentor said links plus screenshots are accepted.
4. New detection, Configure step: "Preview failed" for a valid regex (`closed right now`, span-level, scope verifier). The detection worked after saving; backfill flagged 88 spans.
5. Editing a detection returned `"error": "AI service error"`.
6. Editing a detection (changing only the name) fails on "Update detection" with "Request failed with status code 422"; no field is marked invalid. Creating works.
7. The neatlogs CLI trace reader needs a separate service-account token, so a trace could not be read from the terminal with the project API key.
8. A run that ends with no nudge shows status "success"; nothing marks a silent run without a custom detection.
9. Investigate ("Ask neat AI") assumed two unchecked venues were valid when the fixture data showed they were not.

**Why:** feedback to neatlogs is part of the hackathon relationship; the user wants it collected in one place.

**How to apply:** when the user asks for the neatlogs feedback, draft it from this list, short and to the point, with steps and the project ID `6c876950-22f7-4cc3-b50e-c789cde07355`. See [[runtime-and-whatsapp-scope]].
